title: An Electricity Market Timeline-Aware Probabilistic Approach for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting: Models Comparison and Uncertainty Estimation
content: The growing participation of photovoltaic generation in electricity markets requires forecasts consistent with day-ahead bidding deadlines. These deadlines often prevent the use of the most recent production measurements as forecasting inputs, making realistic data-availability assumptions essential. This study develops a market-aligned forecasting framework combining deterministic prediction and uncertainty estimation for a medium-voltage microgrid hosting 1 MW of distributed photovoltaic capacity. Three models are compared: seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous variables (SARIMAX), random forest, and long short-term (LSTM) networks. Uncertainty is evaluated using a historical baseline and four data-driven approaches: linear quantile regression based on random forest forecasts, quantile regression averaging, quantile regression forests, and conformalized quantile regression forests. Sensitivity analyses examine forecasting configurations and data availability. Random forest achieves the best deterministic performance. Direct forecasting of aggregated production yields an R² of 0.84 and a mean absolute error of 13.36 kW, with accuracy comparable to aggregated single-meter forecasts. Quantile regression forests perform best overall among probabilistic methods, with a mean pinball loss of 9.64 kW and 94% coverage for the nominal 90% prediction interval. Conformalization improves calibration overall but not consistently under challenging conditions. These results support uncertainty-aware day-ahead scheduling under realistic market constraints.
